meta.scope: Demonstration of an architecture assessment for an order application. No user code or service was accessed.
meta.coverage: All 20 dimensions are shown. Synthetic evidence demonstrates traceability, not repository inspection.
exclusions: Real infrastructure, user interface, and data.
Execution of product tests, queries, load, or migrations.
limitations: Evidence E001 through E009 is fictional.
No claim is made about real capacity, security, savings, or agent success.
Canonical terms illustrate decisions; no user repository was inspected.

context.label: Concurrent access
context.value: 120 illustrative active sessions; requests per second are unknown.

context.label: Data and growth
context.value: Volume, distribution, retention, and growth projections are not defined.

context.label: Deployment
context.value: One principal application and a relational database.

context.label: Criticality
context.value: Order integrity matters; availability and recovery targets are not agreed.

questions: Must the ERP confirm the order before the order is considered valid?
What workload and latency, error, and recovery targets represent the actual business need?
What growth horizon and budget could justify a topology change?

verdict.headline: Preserve simplicity. Protect the boundaries.
verdict.summary: In this example, the main risk is order confirmation and integration recovery, not the absence of microservices. The proposed evolution protects the business flow and establishes measurements before distributing the architecture.
verdict.current_fit: The structure is plausible for the illustrative context. Integration has a material gap; capacity and operational requirements have not been demonstrated.
verdict.future_fit: Start with explicit contracts, repeatable verification, and a baseline. Extract components only when scale, isolation, or autonomy justify the cost.

dimensions.title: Fitness for purpose and sufficiency
dimensions.explanation: The topology appears proportionate to the example product. Operational sufficiency still depends on requirements and measurements.

dimensions.title: Domain model and Bounded Contexts
dimensions.explanation: Orders and Billing appear to be distinct capabilities, but their interface does not protect internal implementation. This alone does not establish separate Bounded Contexts.

dimensions.title: Component Cohesion and Component Coupling
dimensions.explanation: An import of internal pricing code creates Component Coupling that can make a local pricing change affect Billing.

dimensions.title: Code design and refactorability
dimensions.explanation: The illustrative calculations have tests and explicit monetary representation. This is not an assessment of all source code.

dimensions.title: Deployment topology
dimensions.explanation: One principal application keeps operation simple. No requirement demonstrates a need to distribute every module.

dimensions.title: APIs and integration
dimensions.explanation: An error response may hide a committed order. The example does not demonstrate protection against repeated business effects.

dimensions.title: Data modeling and integrity
dimensions.explanation: Foreign keys and explicit monetary types are concrete safeguards to preserve in the fictional schema.

dimensions.title: Persistence, ORM, and concurrency
dimensions.explanation: There is no evidence of generated SQL, contention, or query cost from which to judge persistence adequacy or isolation behavior.

dimensions.title: Events and distributed consistency
dimensions.explanation: The local write and external integration do not share an atomic commit. A Transactional Outbox can close the local state/publication-intent gap, but external effects still need protection.

dimensions.title: Capacity, performance, and scalability
dimensions.explanation: Active sessions do not establish throughput or capacity. Workload, percentiles, and resource utilization are missing.

dimensions.title: Reliability and recovery
dimensions.explanation: There is no evidence of successful restoration, failure tolerance, or agreed recovery objectives.

dimensions.title: Security and privacy
dimensions.explanation: Authorization, tenant isolation, and secret management are not demonstrated in this scenario.

dimensions.title: Testing and testability
dimensions.explanation: Calculation tests are useful, but the example does not cover the critical integration failure and duplicate-command behavior.

dimensions.title: Build, delivery, and dependencies
dimensions.explanation: A build recipe and lockfile are declared. Execution from a clean environment remains unverified.

dimensions.title: Observability and operations
dimensions.explanation: The example lacks useful correlation between an ERP error and the associated order state.

dimensions.title: Economics and total cost
dimensions.explanation: Without consumption, bills, or operating effort, there is no basis for quantifying savings.

dimensions.title: User interface and experience
dimensions.explanation: The user interface was not inspected. Accessibility and experience cannot be assessed.

dimensions.title: Team, documentation, and learning
dimensions.explanation: The stated team size does not demonstrate ownership, onboarding effectiveness, or knowledge distribution.

dimensions.title: Agent legibility
dimensions.explanation: The entry map helps locate the process, but leaves setup and test state implicit.

dimensions.title: Agent execution and verification
dimensions.explanation: Agent execution was not tested. Setup gaps suggest a risk, not a measured success or failure rate.

strengths.title: Simple operations
strengths.explanation: One principal application avoids multiplying deployments and network contracts without a demonstrated need.

strengths.title: Schema integrity
strengths.explanation: Keys and monetary precision are explicit safeguards that must survive refactoring.

strengths.title: Tested rule examples
strengths.explanation: Calculation tests provide a starting point for behavior-preserving changes to module boundaries.

findings.title: A committed order can appear to fail
findings.observation: In the fictional flow, the order write commits before the ERP call. An external timeout becomes an error response even though the order already exists.
findings.impact: The user may retry without knowing the order was committed. The risk is a duplicate business effect, not just a poor error message.
findings.recommendation: Protect end-to-end correctness by defining confirmation semantics. If deferred integration is allowed, persist the order and publication intent in one local transaction, then deliver with an explicit idempotency and recovery contract.
findings.tradeoff: Adds pending state, recovery processing, and queue visibility. It does not by itself require a broker or microservices.
alternatives: Keep synchronous integration with explicit state and recovery semantics when external confirmation is mandatory.
Use an existing transactional job mechanism if it provides the required guarantees.
findings.effort: Medium, relative: touches the write path, response contract, and recovery. No calendar estimate is available.
findings.why_now: The ambiguity affects the main business flow and order integrity in the example.
findings.when_not: Do not introduce asynchronous confirmation when ERP approval is required for order validity; redesign the confirmation protocol instead.
findings.validation: Proposed isolated Integration Test: ERP timeout, duplicate input, and resumed delivery. Assert end-to-end correctness using final local and external state. Not run.
findings.acceptance: Under the agreed effect boundary: one business effect per command, explicit integration state, and observable recovery. This is a proposed criterion, not an achieved guarantee.
findings.rollback: Keep schema and read-path compatibility. Drain or reconcile pending intents before disabling the worker; do not delete already-used outbox records.
findings.decision_statement: End-to-end correctness is not protected by the local commit alone, E002. Clarify confirmation semantics before selecting a recovery mechanism.

findings.title: Billing depends on Order internals
findings.observation: Billing directly imports the internal pricing implementation from the Orders module.
findings.impact: An internal refactoring can require changes outside the module. The problem is a fragile boundary, not the number of files.
findings.recommendation: Reduce Component Coupling by defining the required public capability and moving the dependency to its contract. Protect internal imports with a focused architectural fitness function.
findings.tradeoff: Introduces a contract to maintain. Avoid a generic interface or pass-through layer with no useful responsibility.
alternatives: Reassess whether both capabilities belong to one model and should be consolidated.
Share a stable domain concept with explicit ownership, without exposing internal services.
findings.effort: Small to medium, depending on the number of callers, which has not been measured.
findings.why_now: The illustrative code already crosses the intended module boundary.
findings.when_not: Do not separate responsibilities artificially when they belong to one model and legitimately change together.
findings.validation: Inspect callers and run Contract Tests and calculation tests. A proposed import rule checks Component Coupling at the source boundary; it has not been executed.
findings.acceptance: Billing uses only the agreed public interface. Internal pricing changes do not alter unrelated contracts.
findings.rollback: Keep a compatible temporary adapter until callers have migrated.
findings.decision_statement: Component Coupling crosses the intended public boundary, E004. Route the dependency through the required public capability before considering deployment changes.

findings.title: Environment setup depends on implicit knowledge
findings.observation: The example recipe does not define fixtures, data reset, or resources isolated per execution.
findings.impact: Developers and agents can verify different states, interfere with each other, or fail before exercising the intended behavior.
findings.recommendation: Document and implement the minimum diagnostic, setup, seed, and reset recipe needed for a deterministic oracle. Keep one authoritative instruction source.
findings.tradeoff: Fixtures and procedures need maintenance alongside the product. A full environment platform is unnecessary unless scale justifies it.
alternatives: Start with one disposable environment per execution.
Use the existing integration environment with isolated schemas and resource identifiers after checking its limits.
findings.effort: Medium, relative to the external services and data required.
findings.why_now: The gap prevents a confident assessment of execution readiness.
findings.when_not: Do not invest in complex parallelism when one isolated execution meets the team workflow.
findings.validation: Start from a clean environment and verify one synthetic journey twice, including reset, against the same deterministic oracle. Proposed only; no product command was run.
findings.acceptance: The recipe states prerequisites, emits actionable failure messages, and reproduces the expected synthetic state without production secrets.
findings.rollback: Preserve the previous recipe during validation; discard only explicitly owned temporary resources.
findings.decision_statement: A deterministic oracle cannot be reproduced reliably without controlled initial state, E005. Define setup, synthetic fixtures, and safe reset before claiming agent readiness.

findings.title: Failures lack complete correlation
findings.observation: The fictional integration logs do not link the incoming request, order, and ERP delivery attempt.
findings.impact: An operator may see an error without being able to identify the state that needs recovery.
findings.recommendation: Make end-to-end correctness observable by propagating correlation identifiers and recording relevant sanitized state transitions. Define an operational lookup for the flow.
findings.tradeoff: Adds a logging convention and storage cost. Avoid sensitive payloads and uncontrolled cardinality.
alternatives: Use existing tracing if it spans the relevant flow.
Start with consistent structured logs before expanding the observability platform.
findings.effort: Small relative to this example flow; actual volume and platform costs are not measured.
findings.why_now: Integration recovery requires identifying the affected business state.
findings.when_not: Do not replace the observability tool if appropriate instrumentation in the existing one resolves the problem.
findings.validation: Simulate an authorized failure and trace its identifier to the order and delivery attempt. Confirm end-to-end correctness using persisted state, not logs alone.
findings.acceptance: An operator identifies current state and the next recovery action from the request, without secret values in logs.
findings.rollback: Revert new instrumentation without changing business data; preserve compatibility for log consumers.
findings.decision_statement: End-to-end correctness cannot be diagnosed from unlinked logs, E009. Connect the request, order, and delivery attempt before replacing the observability platform.

findings.title: The scaling decision still needs measurements
findings.observation: The scenario supplies an illustrative session count, but no request mix, throughput, latency, or saturation measurements.
findings.impact: There is no sound basis to choose query tuning, more resources, a worker, or distribution. This is not evidence that the application is slow.
findings.recommendation: Establish whether the topology is fit for purpose by agreeing Quality Attribute Scenarios and collecting a representative baseline before changing topology for performance.
findings.tradeoff: Requires preparation and measurement effort. It does not require generating load in production.
alternatives: Use existing telemetry when representative and authorized.
For an experimental product, temporarily accept uncertainty with an explicit reassessment trigger.
findings.effort: Medium, depending on fixtures, environment, and available metrics.
findings.why_now: The growth decision depends on these data; architecture need not change before they exist.
findings.when_not: Do not start an extensive load-testing program without material growth or risk; use proportionate verification.
findings.validation: Define environment, journey mix, data, duration, warm-up, peaks, percentiles, and errors. Run only when authorized. Assess fit for purpose against the agreed target, not an invented threshold.
findings.acceptance: The record distinguishes offered load, completed throughput, latency, and saturation and states the operating range to which the result applies.
findings.rollback: Stop load at safety limits; remove only synthetic data and resources created for the test.
findings.decision_statement: Whether this topology is fit for purpose at peak load remains unknown, E001 and E007. Establish a representative baseline before recommending distribution.

scenarios.environment: A simulated integration with synthetic data.
scenarios.response: Expose explicit state and recover without duplicate protected effects.
scenarios.observed: The example suggests a risk; the scenario was not executed.

scenarios.environment: Orders and Billing modules in the illustrative application.
scenarios.response: Preserve public contracts and avoid unrelated changes.

diagrams.title: The system in context
diagrams.description: A fictional order application stores relational data and integrates with an external ERP. Deployment boundaries are not inferred from directory names.

diagrams.title: Layers and interfaces in the main flow
diagrams.description: These components show runtime responsibilities, not a source dependency proof. Interface Adapters translate input; a Use Case coordinates order rules and persistence. A real assessment must verify these relationships in the code.

diagrams.title: The failure path that matters
diagrams.description: Illustrative sequence: an external error occurs after the local commit. Boxes are numbered flow steps, not components calling each other directly. The ERP result does not undo the earlier commit.

diagrams.title: Proposed evolution: a Transactional Outbox
diagrams.description: Conditional on accepting deferred integration. The order and publication intent commit in the same local transaction. A worker retries delivery; idempotency and reconciliation remain necessary. This does not require distributing every domain.

diagram_gaps: There is insufficient information to reconstruct infrastructure, trust boundaries, a full schema, or a verified Context Map. A real assessment must add these views when relevant.

options.title: Keep the current structure
preconditions: Explicitly accept and record the current flow risks.
options.trigger: Reassess when impact, agreed growth, or a recovery requirement becomes clear.
options.tradeoff: The comparison baseline, not a recommendation to ignore F001.

options.title: Evolve without distributing everything
benefits: Protects public domain contracts and verification.
costs: Adds integration state and a worker.
Requires tests, reconciliation, and boundary discipline.
preconditions: Verify durable publication intent and the effect boundary.
options.trigger: After the baseline, determine whether the worker needs independent resources or deployment.
options.tradeoff: Resolve concrete risks before increasing distribution.

options.title: Extract selected services
benefits: May isolate a specific workload or failure.
May support independent deployment where needed.
costs: Adds contracts, operations, and partial failures.
Does not by itself guarantee better performance or lower cost.
preconditions: Explicit ownership, observability, and data boundaries.
options.trigger: Only after measurements show that local improvements cannot meet the relevant requirement.
options.tradeoff: One targeted extraction may be useful; comprehensive microservices have no demonstrated justification in this example.

actions: Agree the meaning of a confirmed order and ERP failure handling.
Add Characterization Tests for confirmation, timeout, and repeated input.
roadmap.effort: Small to medium, depending on the external contract.
roadmap.acceptance: Define expected cases and final states before changing behavior.
roadmap.rollback: No product change in this step; preserve assessment records.

roadmap.title: Make integration recoverable
actions: Persist durable intent when the contract allows deferred processing.
Implement idempotency, retry limits, and reconciliation.
Add correlation across request, order, and delivery.
roadmap.acceptance: Failure and recovery do not duplicate the protected effect and leave queryable state.
roadmap.rollback: Retain compatible reads and drain or reconcile pending intents before rollback.

roadmap.title: Establish boundaries and a repeatable environment
actions: Publish the pricing capability consumed by Billing.
Define setup, seed, reset, and verifiable commands.
roadmap.owner: Module owners and developer experience owner
roadmap.effort: Medium, depending on callers and local services.
roadmap.acceptance: A synthetic journey works from a clean environment and forbidden internal imports are detected.
roadmap.rollback: Preserve compatible adapters and the previous setup recipe during verification.

roadmap.title: Measure before extracting services
actions: Collect a baseline from telemetry or an authorized isolated test.
Compare local tuning, resource changes, and selective extraction.
roadmap.effort: Medium, bounded by actual growth and risk.
roadmap.acceptance: The scaling decision includes environment, workload, throughput, latency, errors, and cost.
roadmap.rollback: Stop the experiment at safety limits and clean up owned synthetic resources.

evidence.observation: Illustrative assumptions: order product, five engineers, 120 peak active sessions. RPS, SLOs, growth, and budget are not measured or agreed.
In the fictional implementation, the order commits before the ERP call. An exception from that call produces HTTP 500. The example does not demonstrate deduplication of repeated input.
The fictional schema uses foreign keys and decimal monetary types. These safeguards alone do not prevent duplicate business commands.
Billing imports the internal pricing implementation from Orders instead of using a public capability contract.
The fictional documentation explains process startup, but not fixtures, state reset, or resource isolation for two sessions.
The scenario includes order calculation tests. It does not include a final-state test after an ERP timeout or repeated business command.
No load profiles, latency measurements, contention data, incident history, or cost records were supplied. No product execution was performed.
The fictional deployment has one main application and a relational database. A lockfile and build recipe are declared; the recipe was not executed.
The fictional logs do not link the external call, order, and incoming request through a shared correlation identifier.

glossary.definition: The explicit boundary within which a particular domain model and its language are consistent.
Source code dependencies point toward higher-level policy, not outward toward implementation details.
The Clean Architecture policy layer containing the most general enterprise business rules.
Application-specific business rules that orchestrate Entities and the steps needed to achieve an application goal.
Code that converts representations between policy and external delivery or persistence mechanisms.
Principles governing dependencies among components and their stability.
Persist business state and a publication intent in the same local transaction, then deliver that intent separately.
A common community term for making repeated processing attempts produce one observable effect within an explicitly defined boundary.
A point where behavior can be changed without editing the code at that point; an enabling point controls which behavior is used.
Refactoring changes internal structure while preserving the behavior included in the agreed contract.
A verification rule whose verdict is reproducible under controlled inputs, state, and explicitly stated assumptions.
Repeating the same identified operation has the same intended effect as applying it once, within the declared contract and retention scope.
The percentile below which approximately 95 percent of observations fall for the stated sample and conditions.
A measurable service-level objective agreed for a defined scope and time window.

concept_applications.decision: Whether peak operation is fit for purpose is unresolved by a session count, E001 and E007. Keep the topology while establishing a baseline.
concept_applications.action: Assess fit for purpose against agreed workload and response targets before extracting services.
concept_applications.verification: Record offered load, completed throughput, latency, errors, and saturation in an authorized environment.

concept_applications.decision: Component Coupling exposes Order implementation to Billing through an internal import, E004. Repair the contract boundary first.
concept_applications.action: Reduce Component Coupling by publishing the required capability and moving callers to it.
concept_applications.verification: A focused import rule rejects the internal dependency while Contract Tests protect behavior.

concept_applications.decision: The deterministic oracle needs a controlled initial state, which the example setup recipe does not define, E005.
concept_applications.action: Provide synthetic fixtures and safe reset so the deterministic oracle can be repeated from a clean state.
concept_applications.verification: Run the same journey twice after reset and check the same final-state assertions; this is a proposed check.

concept_applications.decision: End-to-end correctness spans the local commit, ERP effect, and user-visible response, E002. Clarify confirmation and recovery before adding infrastructure.
concept_applications.action: Protect end-to-end correctness with explicit states, repeat-safe effects, and correlated attempts.
concept_applications.verification: Exercise timeout and replay in isolation, then inspect both the local record and the protected external effect.

concept_applications.decision: A Transactional Outbox is a conditional solution to the local write/publication-intent gap, E002, when deferred integration is valid.
concept_applications.action: Use the Transactional Outbox only after approval of deferred confirmation; keep idempotency and reconciliation as separate obligations.
concept_applications.verification: Fail after the local commit, resume delivery, and verify durable intent plus the protected sink effect. Not executed.

concept_applications.decision: The Dependency Rule cannot be judged from the runtime component diagram alone. The source-import graph of the policy and adapters is not supplied.
concept_applications.action: Inspect inward and outward source dependencies before classifying compliance; do not infer a violation from an outward runtime call.
concept_applications.verification: Read the concrete policy imports and composition interfaces at a known revision.

concept_applications.decision: Event Sourcing is not required by the demonstrated outbox use case. No requirement makes the event history the authoritative domain state.
concept_applications.action: Keep the existing state model; reconsider only when an authoritative event history serves a concrete requirement.
concept_applications.verification: Verify that documentation does not mislabel publication intents as an event-sourced system.

concept_applications.decision: The smallest reversible move is a compatible capability boundary and a clarified confirmation contract, not wholesale service extraction.
concept_applications.action: Stage the smallest reversible move behind compatible interfaces, preserving read and recovery paths.
concept_applications.verification: Check existing contracts before switching callers; stop or recover forward if data compatibility is lost.

concept_applications.decision: Separate Orders and Billing modules do not establish a Bounded Context boundary. Model vocabulary, invariants, and ownership need confirmation.
concept_applications.action: Compare the two models and their Ubiquitous Language before deciding whether to separate or consolidate them.
concept_applications.verification: Record the domain meanings and integration relationship in a Context Map if distinct contexts are established.
